headline: Disney's new CTO led AI startup it accused of copyright infringement
summary: Karandeep Anand, formerly of Character.AI, is now Disney's chief technology officer, overseeing enterprise tech and AI platforms.
details: Disney has appointed Karandeep Anand, the former CEO of AI company Character.AI, as its new Chief Technology Officer. Anand will report directly to Disney CEO Josh D'Amaro and will be responsible for enterprise technology and the company's data and AI platforms.
Anand's appointment comes as Disney CEO Josh D'Amaro emphasizes the company's role as a technology leader, with the Disney+ streaming service and app being central to its future strategy.

This move is notable because Disney sent a cease and desist letter to Character.AI in September 2025, accusing the platform of offering chatbots based on its characters and posing risks to children. Character.AI had also faced lawsuits related to underage users at the time.
Despite the previous legal dispute, Disney's statement highlighted Anand's "rare mix of experience across infrastructure, consumer technology and AI," and his "enthusiasm and respect for Disney."
Disney also announced that Adam Smith, previously the chief product and technology officer for Disney Entertainment and ESPN, will move to Chairman of Direct-to-Consumer for Disney Entertainment.

The company's willingness to hire Anand, despite past accusations, suggests a strategic focus on leveraging AI expertise, potentially outweighing previous concerns about generative AI's risks or intellectual property issues.
caption:
Disney hires former CEO of AI firm it previously accused of copyright infringement and endangering children.

Disney has appointed Karandeep Anand, the former CEO of AI company Character.AI, as its new Chief Technology Officer. Anand will report directly to Disney CEO Josh D'Amaro and will be responsible for enterprise technology and the company's data and AI platforms.

Anand's appointment comes as Disney CEO Josh D'Amaro emphasizes the company's role as a technology leader, with the Disney+ streaming service and app being central to its future strategy.

This move is notable because Disney sent a cease and desist letter to Character.AI in September 2025, accusing the platform of offering chatbots based on its characters and posing risks to children. Character.AI had also faced lawsuits related to underage users at the time.

Despite the previous legal dispute, Disney's statement highlighted Anand's "rare mix of experience across infrastructure, consumer technology and AI," and his "enthusiasm and respect for Disney."

Disney also announced that Adam Smith, previously the chief product and technology officer for Disney Entertainment and ESPN, will move to Chairman of Direct-to-Consumer for Disney Entertainment.

The company's willingness to hire Anand, despite past accusations, suggests a strategic focus on leveraging AI expertise, potentially outweighing previous concerns about generative AI's risks or intellectual property issues.
